title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: makers can build declarative agents with flexible layouts and rich UX components
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap target and keeps documented interactive interfaces separate from the planned feature. The agent controls, preview automation and licensing statements are supported; targeted searches found no documentation resolving the feature-specific gaps.

claims.claim: Copilot UX components provide SPFx-built interactive UI packaged with declarative agents.
claims.quote: A solution can package one or more Copilot UX components - client-side UI components that render inside Microsoft 365 Copilot - together with a declarative agent definition that makes them discoverable and callable from within a Copilot conversation.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: User access controls which organisation members or groups access and install agents and plugins.
claims.quote: Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins. ... Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access selection.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: Preview TCM automation supports applying All users or No users for User access.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne
